{"kind":"proof","text":"For each \(x\in[0,1)\), we have \(x^n\to0\), while \(f_n(1)=1\) for every \(n\). Thus the pointwise limit is
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1,\\1,&x=1.\end{cases}
\]
If \((f_n)\) converged uniformly, its uniform limit would necessarily equal this pointwise limit. For each \(n\ge1\), let \(x_n=2^{-1/n}\). Then \(x_n<1\), so \(f(x_n)=0\), whereas
\[
f_n(x_n)=(2^{-1/n})^n=\frac12.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge \frac12
\]
for every \(n\). This supremum therefore does not tend to \(0\), so \((f_n)\) does not converge uniformly on \([0,1]\).","reason":""}
